subject: ss-neurosurgery
title: Cavernomas and dural fistulas: popcorn MRI, reflux grading and closure

steps.say: Cavernomas are looking like popcorn on MRI with a dark rim of old blood around them. They are enhancing little and they are hiding on angiography. Tumours and AVMs are behaving differently on both studies.
steps.tx: Cavernomas show a **popcorn lesion** core of blood products with a dark hemosiderin rim on MRI, enhance minimally, and hide on angiography, staying angiographically occult, which separates them from AVMs and tumours. The rim is haemosiderin from repeated silent bleeds. Angiographic invisibility is itself a diagnostic clue.

steps.say: Zabramski types are running from fresh haemorrhage to burnt-out calcified lesions. A developmental venous anomaly alongside is left strictly alone. Resecting it is infarcting the brain it is draining.
steps.tx: **Zabramski types** run from acute haemorrhage to calcified burnt-out lesions, and a developmental venous anomaly alongside is left alone because resecting it causes venous infarct of draining brain. The anomaly is the venous drainage of normal tissue. Surgery targets the cavernoma only, never its venous partner.

steps.say: Familial cases are carrying CCM1, CCM2 or CCM3 mutations with many lesions. Relatives are offered gradient-echo MRI screening for silent spots. Spinal imaging is added when symptoms are pointing there.
steps.tx: Familial cavernomas with CCM1 **KRIT1**, CCM2 or CCM3 mutations present with multiple cavernomas, and relatives get gradient-echo MRI screening plus spinal imaging when symptomatic. A single lesion in an older adult is usually sporadic. Multiple lesions in the young trigger genetic counselling and family screening.

steps.say: An accessible cavernoma causing fits is removed with its rusty rim. Taking the rim is improving seizure control markedly. Deep silent ones are watched because each bleed is usually small.
steps.tx: A single accessible cavernoma causing epilepsy undergoes **lesionectomy** with its hemosiderin rim for seizure control, while deep asymptomatic ones are watched because each bleed is usually small. The rim holds epileptogenic iron deposits. Leaving rim behind invites ongoing fits despite clot removal.

steps.say: Brainstem cavernomas are operated only after repeated bleeds have declared danger. Each approach is passing through a mapped safe entry zone. Rebleed risk is balanced against certain new deficit.
steps.tx: **Brainstem cavernoma**s are operated only after 2 symptomatic bleeds via a safe entry zone approach, balancing rebleed risk against certain new deficit. The first bleed is managed conservatively while the patient recovers. A second bleed proves aggressive biology and justifies the risk.

steps.say: Dural fistulas are announcing themselves with pulsing head noise or red bulging eyes. Bleeding is the alarming presentation in cortical-draining types. Grading is resting entirely on venous reflux.
steps.tx: Dural arteriovenous fistulas present with pulsatile tinnitus, orbital congestion or haemorrhage, and the Borden scale with the Cognard scale grade danger by **cortical venous reflux**, with reflux mandating treatment. No reflux means a benign course in most cases. Reflux means the brain veins carry arterial pressure.

vis.alt: Lateral cerebral angiogram showing a large arteriovenous malformation with prominent nidus and dilated draining veins.
vis.caption: Angiography reveals AVM nidus and draining veins while cavernomas stay hidden. Credit: Royonx, CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.say: Fistulas without reflux are watched safely with periodic imaging. Reflux-positive ones are closed through arteries, veins, surgery or radiosurgery. The middle meningeal feeder is the commonest transarterial road.
steps.tx: Transverse-sigmoid fistulas without reflux may be watched, while reflux-positive fistulas are closed by transvenous embolisation, transarterially through the **middle meningeal feeder**, surgically or with radiosurgery. Embolisation aims to disconnect the refluxing vein before pressure damages the brain. Cure is confirmed on delayed angiography.

vis.alt: Diagram showing a microcatheter delivering liquid embolic agent into a vascular nidus through a feeding artery toward the draining vein.
vis.caption: Transarterial embolisation casts the fistula and shunts via microcatheter. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Carotid cavernous fistulas are swelling the eye with chemosis and proptosis. A bruit is heard over the orbit in high-flow types. Traumatic direct ones are closed urgently to save vision.
steps.tx: **Carotid-cavernous fistula**s cause chemosis, proptosis, bruit and ophthalmoplegia, and direct high-flow types after trauma need urgent endovascular closure to save vision. Indirect low-flow types may thrombose alone over months without any intervention. Rising eye pressure with falling vision forces the timetable.

rows: May watch, embolise if eye threatened
